newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER ENJOYS EASY AFTERNOON ON HOME COURT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER ENJOYS EASY AFTERNOON ON HOME COURT.

text.p: Australian Open champion Boris Becker enjoyed a comfortable afternoon's work in his native Germany to reach the quarter-finals of the Stuttgart Open on Thursday.
Becker, who is trying to get back to his best after suffering a serious wrist injury at this year's Wimbledon, produced one of his best performances for months to beat Swede Thomas Enqvist 6-4 7-5.

"That was my best match since Wimbledon," the three-times Wimbledon champion said after his 80-minute victory. "It shows I have broken through the problems with the wrist...I surprised myself how well I played."

The victory delighted his home crowd which included his parents. More importantly, it boosted Becker's chances of qualifying for next month's season-ending world championship in Hanover where he is the reigning champion.

The German's favourite surface is grass where he can use his strong serve-and-volley game to the full, but the fast carpeted courts of the European indoor tournaments at the end of the season come a close second.

With 6,000 Germans cheering his every move in the Stuttgart Schleyerhalle, Becker clinched the first set after a break of serve in the ninth game. Becker made the match-winning break in the 11th game of the second set when Enqvist hit a volley out of court.
The only time Becker's concentration faltered was when he was disturbed by some over-zealous commentators in the television booths behind the court early in the second set.
A quick scowl and a word and the commentators turned down the volume.
Becker said afterwards he was not just a power server stressing variety was as important as speed. But he was clearly relishing the prospect of a few more weeks on the fast indoor courts.
"It is about winning the point. It is not just about breaking the (serving speed) record of Greg Rusedski," he said.
"It is nice to play here because it is my old home. My parents have been popping by every day," the Munich-based player added.
In Friday's quarter-finals, Becker now faces Swede Magnus Gustafsson who beat Australian Mark Woodforde 6-7 6-2 7-6 in the first match of the day.

Andre Agassi, seeded ninth, made sure of his place in the last eight after a straightforward 6-4 6-2 victory over compatriot Richey Reneberg to set up a likely showdown with world number one Pete Sampras.
Sampras faces Spaniard Felix Mantilla later on Thursday.
